subject: Obtain samples of the marginal posterior distrubtions

messages.author: e0ca5a0f7a37b5e8
messages.subject: Obtain samples of the marginal posterior distrubtions
parts:
Dear R-INLA project

How can I obtain multiple samples of the marginal posterior distrubtions of the parameters estimates in an inla() model?

For example, is there an equivalent to model$sims.matrix from the R2WinBUGS package?

Many thanks

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Obtain samples of the marginal posterior distrubtions
parts:
Hi Rachel,
There's an experimental function called inla.posterior.sample that computes a sample from the joint posterior.

The help should give you an idea how to use it.

Best wishes,
Dan

messages.author: e0ca5a0f7a37b5e8
messages.subject: Re: Obtain samples of the marginal posterior distrubtions
parts:
I have a model

y ~ NegBin(mu,r)

log(mu)=log(e) + alpha + beta1*x1 + phi + nu

To compare observed to fitted values, is the following command correct?

yhat <- exp(result$summary.linear.predictor$mean)

where result in my inla model object.

How would I obtain 1000 samples, equivalent to the response, y?

Many thanks for your help

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Obtain samples of the marginal posterior distrubtions
parts:
The question is discussed here

http://www.r-inla.org/faq#TOC-How-can-I-do-predictions-using-INLA-

maybe you want this as well.

http://www.r-inla.org/faq#TOC-How-can-I-compute-cross-validation-or-predictive-measures-of-fit-


if you want to simulate data from the posterior of the model, then you
can use inla.posterior.sample() to get samples and then sample data from
those using the negbin.

H
